title: Customer Reference Program — Weekly Exec Review Readout (Week of 2025-10-24)
content:
Slide 1 — Title
Customer Reference Program — Weekly Exec Review Readout
Week of 2025-10-24
Owners: Camila Reyes (Program), Soojin Lee (Messaging), Tyler Benson (Ops)
Exec sponsors: Stephanie Nguyen (Sales), VP Marketing

Slide 2 — Program goals + success metrics (reminder)
Goal: accelerate late-stage conversion for Dedicated/Private via references + public stories
8–10 week push plan
Success metrics (by end of push):
- 3–5 signed reference agreements
- 2–3 published public case studies (logo + quotes; metrics where possible)
- Reference-call utilization: steady requests/month + short SLA
- Influence: reference usage tagged on late-stage deals + qualitative AE/CS feedback
Notes: continuing to bias for low operational burden on customers (cooldown + do-not-contact enforcement)

Slide 3 — Executive summary (this week)
Wins:
- Northwind: verbal commitment reconfirmed; draft story structure approved internally; architecture diagram in final technical review
- Polaris DevTools: strong quotes secured; willing for reference calls immediately; public logo approval likely (low legal friction)
- Intake workflow: “no surprise asks” rule adopted by Sales leadership; HubSpot tagging draft reviewed by RevOps

Risks:
- Helios Health: legal/compliance redlines still open (anonymization + metric ranges). Could slip past target publication window.
- Atlas Insurance: procurement + support terms gating any public statement; still viable for reference calls only in near term.
- Metrics credibility: Northwind had a transient latency incident during interview window (SUP-3812) — resolved but impacts what we publish.

Asks/Decisions needed this week:
- Approve plan to publish metrics as ranges for Helios (if approved) and to publish Northwind without exact p95 numbers (use validated “before/after” relative statements)
- Confirm incentive selection default for enterprise: conference sponsorship credit vs charitable donation (customer preference)

Slide 4 — Reference pipeline (funnel view)
Current funnel counts (design partner targets = 3–5):
- Candidates identified: 12
- Actively engaged (outreach + qualification): 7
- Verbal commitments (reference calls + case study intent): 4
- Signed consent / reference agreement: 1
- Published case studies: 0 (Northwind scheduled first)

Verbal commitment list (current):
1) Northwind Commerce (Dedicated) — case study + reference calls
2) Helios Health (Private/VPC) — case study pending legal; reference calls likely after approvals
3) Polaris DevTools (Hosted at scale) — reference calls now; case study likely
4) Cascade Customer Support (Hosted + embeddings) — reference calls (guardrails) / no public metrics

Slide 5 — Account-by-account status (top candidates)
Northwind Commerce (Dedicated)
- Story angle: Dedicated capacity + routing/fallback + cost controls via caching/batching; “production reliability without bespoke infra”
- Current stage: Draft narrative in internal review; diagram under SE validation
- What they will do: public logo + 1–2 approved quotes; allow reference calls with guardrails
- Blockers: metric publication scope; ensure post-incident numbers aren’t misleading
- Owner(s): Avery Johnson (AE), Markus Klein (SE), Ethan Wallace (writer)

Helios Health (Private/VPC)
- Story angle: regulated workload, audit logs + KMS, data residency + operational controls
- Current stage: compliance-safe draft language in progress
- Blockers: legal wants anonymization + metric ranges; review window longer than typical (10–15 biz days)
- Owner(s): Hannah Schmitt (CS liaison), Michael Grant (Legal), Soojin Lee (messaging)

Atlas Insurance (Dedicated/Private evaluation)
- Story angle: doc summarization + RAG; migration; eval harness + regression monitoring
- Current stage: “reference-call ready” discovery completed; public case study not approved
- Blockers: procurement + SLA/support terms; competitor displacement sensitivity
- Owner(s): Priyom Das (AE), Rachel Kim (CS), Isabelle Laurent (tracking)

Polaris DevTools (Hosted)
- Story angle: time-to-value + Optimize suggestions (batching/caching) + predictable latency under burst
- Current stage: interview #1 complete; quotes drafted; waiting for lightweight brand approval
- Blockers: none critical; confirm whether they’ll share a single concrete metric (e.g., integration time or cost reduction range)
- Owner(s): Miguel Santos (liaison), Ethan Wallace (writer), Tyler Benson (ops)

Cascade Customer Support (Hosted)
- Story angle: agent assist reliability + “what to avoid” playbook; customer-friendly boundaries
- Current stage: reference-call prep playbook synced with CS
- Blockers: recent escalation history means strict topic boundaries + limited call volume
- Owner(s): Rachel Kim (CS), Tyler Benson (ops)

Aurora Payments (Dedicated interest)
- Story angle: uptime + region constraints; potential partner webinar angle
- Current stage: exploratory; not yet asked for public story
- Blockers: strict policy requirements; need CS health check before asking
- Owner(s): Stephanie Nguyen (sponsor), CS owner TBD

Slide 6 — Pipeline influence (to date)
What we’re measuring (current best-effort; improving):
- “Reference call used” tag on deals (HubSpot property in review)
- “Case study shared” tracked via sales sequence insert + deck link clicks
- Late-stage conversion qualitative feedback from AEs + SEs

Early signals (last 2 weeks, directional):
- Reference-call requests: 3 total (2 Dedicated, 1 Private)
- Reference calls completed: 1 (Atlas-style Q&A format; internal feedback positive but prep needed)
- Deals where references are expected to be used in next 14 days: 4
- Net-new pipeline directly attributed to program: not claimed (too early); focusing on influence tagging vs sourced

Notes:
- We are not counting “logo permission pending” as influence; only when a case study/link/call is actually used
- RevOps request: align on one canonical “influence” definition before we report $ influenced in QBRs

Slide 7 — Published assets status (web + PDF + talk track)
Case study web template:
- Status: implemented in docs site; landing page ready; placeholders staged
- Owner: DevEx + Design (DES-611 / ENG-9401)

Northwind assets (in progress):
- Web page draft: in final internal fact-check
- 1-pager PDF: outline done; design pass next week
- Sales talk track: v0.3 ready; awaiting final proof language on metrics

Polaris assets (in progress):
- Narrative draft: in progress (needs second interview for implementation details)
- Quotes: drafted, pending customer confirmation

Slide 8 — Blockers & mitigations
Blocker: Helios legal/compliance redlines
- Issue: requests for anonymization + “no exact metrics” + longer review window
- Proposed mitigation:
  - Use metric ranges (e.g., “p95 improved by 30–45%”) + disclosure disclaimer
  - Offer alternate format: “customer profile” without logo until legal clears
  - Pre-approve claim language with Legal before we invest in design

Blocker: Northwind metric integrity (post-latency incident)
- Issue: transient p95 spike happened during interview window; risk of publishing inconsistent numbers
- Proposed mitigation:
  - Publish only metrics measured over agreed stable window (last 14 days) OR use relative language without specific p95
  - Include a standard disclaimer on measurement method and timeframe
  - Ensure SE signs off on any performance claims (Markus/Simran)

Blocker: Reference customer fatigue / overuse
- Issue: multiple AEs asking same customer; risk of burnout
- Mitigation:
  - Enforce cooldown policy (target: max 2 calls/month/customer)
  - Central scheduling via Marketing Ops; do-not-contact list enforced
  - Post-call logging required to prevent duplicate asks

Slide 9 — Next-week milestones (week of 2025-10-28)
Northwind (publish-first plan):
- Finalize technical validation + claims checklist (by Wed)
- Customer legal/brand final review window closes (Thu)
- Publish web page + internal enablement announcement (Fri)

Helios:
- Send revised consent language + anonymized draft (Mon)
- Confirm whether they will allow: (a) logo, (b) named quotes, (c) metric ranges only

Polaris:
- Schedule interview #2 (implementation + results framing)
- Confirm willingness for public logo + one concrete “time-to-value” statement

Ops + enablement:
- Finalize HubSpot properties + Slack channel routing for reference requests (RevOps review)
- Update reference-call brief template with “what we learned” from first call (avoid list + questions bank)

Slide 10 — Requests to exec team (decisions + help)
Decision 1: Metrics publication posture
- Option A: Prefer exact metrics when possible; otherwise use ranges w/ disclaimer
- Option B: Standardize on ranges to reduce legal friction + speed publication
Recommendation: Option A (exact when approved; default to ranges) to preserve credibility while keeping velocity

Decision 2: Incentive default
- Current approved options: conference sponsorship credit / extended Optimize trial / charitable donation
Recommendation: set default = conference sponsorship credit; allow donation upon request for regulated orgs

Help needed:
- Stephanie: align AEs on “no surprise ask” policy + require intake form for all reference requests
- VP Marketing: confirm distribution priority (blog vs docs vs sales outbound first) for Northwind launch

Slide 11 — Appendix: weekly scoreboard (snapshot)
Week ending: 2025-10-24
- New candidate nominations this week: 2
- Qualification calls completed: 3
- New verbal commitments: 1 (Cascade for reference calls)
- Signed agreements added: 0 (Northwind pending)
- Drafts in progress: 2 (Northwind, Polaris)
- Legal reviews active: 1 (Helios)

Operational notes:
- SLA target for scheduling reference calls once approved: 5 business days (depends on customer availability)
- Post-call logging compliance: ~60% (needs reinforcement)

Slide 12 — Appendix: open questions
- Should we allow “named customer, no logo” as a middle ground, or does that confuse credibility?
- For Private stories: do we need a separate compliance-safe template (language + proof requirements) vs reusing standard template?
- Who owns long-term reference governance after the 8–10 week push (Marketing Ops vs CS Ops)?

Speaker notes (for Camila)
- Keep exec review focused on: (1) publish Northwind first, (2) unblock Helios legal, (3) protect customer bandwidth.
- Avoid committing to influenced $ until tagging is stable; ask RevOps to finalize definition + required fields.
- If Northwind legal review slips, recommend publishing Polaris first (faster approvals) to avoid losing momentum.
